ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all ultimate beneficial owners, directors, prescribed officers, and authorized representatives against the FIC list of domestic prominent influential persons, the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the South African Targeted Financial Sanctions List; enhanced due diligence under FICA s 21G for foreign PEPs; ongoing transaction monitoring, adverse-media review, and filing of suspicious transaction reports with the Financial Intelligence Centre as required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services portal (https://eservices.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be submitted in the Latin script or in a transliterated Romanized form; the name may be expressed in English, Afrikaans, or any of the 12 official South African languages, but must be transliterated into Latin characters. The legal form suffix '(Pty) Ltd' must appear as the final element of the corporate name. Names must not be offensive, misleading, or create a false impression of connection with the government, a government agency, a foreign state, or a regulated profession.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant receives a CIPC e-Services notice stating the statutory ground of refusal under s 11 of the Companies Act, 2008. Procedure: (1) remedy the defect and file a fresh name reservation application (Form CoR 9.1) on the CIPC transactional portal; (2) alternatively, within 20 business days of rejection, lodge an application with the Companies Tribunal under s 160 of the Companies Act, 2008, submitting Form CTR-NOT together with a founding affidavit and the rejection notification; (3) CIPC may, on good cause shown, extend an approved reservation for a further period not exceeding 20 business days; (4) if the administrative remedies are exhausted, the applicant may pursue judicial review in the High Court of South Africa.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only where the service provider supplies a physical street address in South Africa at which statutory records, the Memorandum of Incorporation, and meeting minutes are retained and where legal process may be served, as required by s 23 of the Companies Act, 2008. A pure virtual mailbox address without physical record-keeping presence does not satisfy the statutory mandate. For a restaurant operation, the licensed restaurant premises will constitute the primary commercial substance, and a serviced registered office is acceptable only as a supplementary administrative address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - approximately 85% cumulative likelihood of unannounced physical inspections during the first 12 months of operation, including municipal Environmental Health inspections for the Certificate of Acceptability, Department of Employment and Labour inspections for occupational health and UIF/COIDA compliance, local fire-safety inspections, and SARS field audits targeting POS cash-flow verification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss. 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 19, 66 and 69; Companies Regulations, 2011, Forms CoR 9.4, CoR 14.1 and CoR 14.3
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), a juristic entity established under s.185 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) filed in terms of s.13(1) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a private company (Pty) Ltd; authorised shares, including no-par-value shares, may be allotted with zero paid-up capital. No escrow account is required under the Companies Act. The MOI must state the authorised share capital and the first board must confirm the issued shares as fully paid upon subscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the Company adopts the Memorandum of Incorporation filed with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission and confirms the subscription of the issued share capital by the initial shareholders; (2) the registered office of the Company is [Address], Republic of South Africa, approved for all statutory notices and service; (3) [Name] and [Name] are appointed as directors, with [Name] as Managing Director and [Name] as Company Secretary; (4) any director is authorised to instruct CIPC and SARS agents, open bank accounts, and certify copies of this resolution. This resolution is effective upon the Company's registration certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services Company Name Reservation window (www.cipc.co.za)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary search of the CIPC company and trade mark databases to verify that the proposed name is not identical to an existing name. File Form CoR 9.4 (Notice of Reservation of Name) selecting the company name with the suffix '(Pty) Ltd'. Await the CIPC decision under ss. 11 and 12. A reserved name is valid for 20 business days; if it expires before incorporation, a fresh reservation application is required.
required_dossiers: Certified identity document or passport of the applicant
Proof of proposed registered office address
Power of attorney if an agent files on behalf of the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as confusingly similar, offensive, or contrary to s.11, file a revised CoR 9.4 with alternative names or submit formal representations to CIPC seeking reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Memorandum of Incorporation and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC-accredited incorporation attorney or registered CIPC service provider acting as agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI in accordance with s.15, specifying the authorised share capital, board composition, quorum and any restrictive conditions. Secure the written consent of each first director under s.69 and certified identity documents. Obtain the registered office consent from the building owner where the company does not own the premises. The MOI must not contain any provision inconsistent with the Companies Act.
required_dossiers: Director consent forms executed under s.69
Certified copies of identity documents or passports of all directors and incorporators
Registered office consent from the premises owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC queries the MOI, revise the non-compliant provisions, file a replacement MOI and comply with any notice issued by the CIPC before the registration deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) with MOI
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC Company Registration Directorate, e-Services Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into CIPC e-Services, select 'Register a Company', complete Form CoR 14.1 Notice of Incorporation, upload the final MOI, the name reservation certificate, certified identity documents and director consents. Submit the application through the transaction cart and await compliance screening under ss. 13 and 14.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond through the CIPC correspondence module within the period specified in the query; correct any defective exhibits and re-submit, or file a fresh application if the existing filing is rejected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Filing Fees, Statutory Registration and Issuance of Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC Registration Administration and e-Services payment gateway
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Settle the incorporation fee of R125 plus the R50 name reservation fee (total approximately USD 10, subject to exchange and tariff changes) through the CIPC payment gateway. Upon confirmation of payment and successful compliance screening, CIPC issues Form CoR 14.3 Certificate of Registration, setting out the company name, registration number and date of incorporation. Download the certificate and the certified MOI from the transaction history page.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not generated within the service standard, retrieve it from CIPC 'My Transactions'; where the certificate is defective, file a correction request under the CIPC Return of Corrections procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Tax Registration (Income Tax, VAT and Employer Taxes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling Registration Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax within 21 business days of incorporation to obtain an income tax reference number. Register for VAT as a compulsory vendor where taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed R1 million in any 12-month period, or on a voluntary basis. Register as an employer for PAYE, UIF and SDL within 21 business days of becoming an employer. Appointments with a SARS branch may be required for FICA verification.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Incorporation and certified directors' identity documents
SARS registration forms IT77 (income tax), VAT101 (VAT) and EMP101 (employer)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS imposes a verification hold, attend the nearest SARS branch with certified documents, complete the verification at a self-help kiosk, and obtain the tax reference numbers; unresolved disputes may be raised with the SARS branch manager.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) - eFiling portal (https://www.sars.gov.za; https://efiling.sars.gov.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A (Pty) Ltd is incorporated with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC); CIPC transmits incorporation data to SARS, after which the company activates its eFiling profile to obtain the income tax reference number. VAT registration via Form VAT101 is compulsory once taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any 12 consecutive months, with voluntary registration available at ZAR 50,000; PAYE registration is required when employees are appointed; import and export activity requires a SARS Customs code. A foreign external company carrying on business through a South African branch registers the branch with CIPC, obtains a non-resident income tax reference number, and registers for VAT if the branch's taxable turnover exceeds the threshold; non-resident suppliers of electronic services use the dedicated s 54E VAT Act registration channel.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa has no check-the-box classification election; a (Pty) Ltd is statutorily a resident company taxed at entity level. Available elections include the headquarter company regime (s 9I, Income Tax Act 58 of 1962), voluntary VAT registration at ZAR 50,000 (s 23(2), VAT Act 89 of 1991), and the micro business turnover tax election (Sixth Schedule). The OECD BEPS Action 2 hybrid mismatch neutralisation rules apply mandatorily to years of assessment commencing on or after 1 January 2024 and are not elective.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933, as delegated by the National Treasury
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand is convertible for current-account transactions through SARB authorised dealers but remains subject to partial exchange control. Current-account payments for trade, services, royalties, interest, and dividends may be remitted once the underlying commercial documentation is verified by an authorised dealer; no SARB pre-approval is ordinarily required for legitimate current-account payments by a resident (Pty) Ltd. Capital-account transfers, particularly outward capital remittances by residents, are controlled and generally require FinSurv permission or must fall within an approved allowance. Inward foreign direct investment is freely permitted and must be reported for balance-of-payments purposes. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders in the form of ordinary dividends is permitted through an authorised dealer, subject to: formal board declaration; the Companies Act 2008 solvency and liquidity test; dividends tax at 20% withheld and paid to SARS; and retention of the full dividend resolution, financial statements, and inward capital-import evidence. Additional transfer-pricing and economic-substance documentation should be maintained to reduce bank and SARS friction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SARB Exchange Control Regulations, export proceeds from goods shipped from South Africa must be received in South Africa through an authorised dealer within 180 days from the date of shipment, unless a longer period is specifically approved by FinSurv. The full 100% of exported goods proceeds must be repatriated and surrendered through the local banking system; no portion may be retained offshore without FinSurv authorisation. Where payments are received in foreign currency, they must be converted into Rand or credited to a bank-approved foreign-currency account only for a permitted temporary period and must ultimately be brought onshore or applied strictly in accordance with the authorised dealer's instructions. This regime applies to the condiment-export side of the hotpot chain. Import-related settlement obligations are governed separately by the Customs and Excise Act and SARS import declarations (SAD500).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary clearing rail. Offshore fintech EMIs and digital payment platforms are not SARB authorised dealers, cannot access the national ZAR settlement system (SAMOS via BankservAfrica), and cannot independently perform exchange-control clearance or capital-import reporting. They may be used only as ancillary card-issuing, POS aggregation, or FX conversion layers, but all inbound equity, trade settlements, and repatriation flows must pass through a locally licensed bank with authorised-dealer status. The use of unlicensed foreign EMI accounts for operating cash would be a regulatory red flag and should be avoided.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) requires the bank to verify its client, the beneficial owners, and the authority of signatories. For a foreign-owned newly incorporated (Pty) Ltd, at least one natural-person director, senior manager, or duly authorised signatory with original mandate documents will normally be required to attend an in-person interview at a South African branch, or at a foreign office of an international bank with correspondent vetting where the bank permits. Purely remote account opening is possible only if the bank's FICA-compliant electronic KYC permits video verification of identity and source of funds; however, capital escrow and cross-border remittance accounts are subject to enhanced due diligence and effectively require physical or attested mandate authentication. The bank will also require the company incorporation certificate, Memorandum of Incorporation, register of directors and shareholders, tax clearance status, and proof of registered address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Company registration address is a leased hospitality premises and beneficial owners are non-resident individuals without a South African credit footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified lease agreement, municipal rates or utility account in the company's name, restaurant operating licence / liquor-related permits, passport copies, proof of foreign residential address, background check, and foreign bank reference for all non-resident beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive full-service restaurant expected to generate high volumes of cash bank deposits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Integrated POS terminal daily Z-reports, cash-up reconciliation sheets, daily banking slips, supplier invoices, SARS VAT return reconciliations, cash-handling standard operating procedures, and an AML/CTF compliance manual with threshold reporting procedures for cash deposits above R24,999.99.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner connected to a high-risk jurisdiction, politically exposed person status, or ambiguous source of wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport and national proof of address, source of wealth statement, source of funds file, entity ownership chart, share register, professional references, sanctions screening records, and where applicable an independent audit or legal opinion confirming no PEP prohibition.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound equity subscription or shareholder loan from abroad perceived as suspicious round-tripping or capitalisation without clear business purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder resolution, board resolution, share subscription agreement, shareholder loan agreement on arm's-length terms, detailed use-of-proceeds projection, company business plan, inward SWIFT MT103 record, SARB/authorised-dealer capital-import reference, and audited or reviewed financial projections.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Import disbursements to China for hotpot condiments and equipment through intermediary trading vehicles
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original commercial invoices, pro-forma invoices, bills of lading or airway bills, packing lists, certificate of origin, SARS customs import declaration (SAD500), tax invoices, commercial contract, and the corresponding SWIFT MT103 or letter of credit transaction record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dividends or repayment of shareholder loans requested in the first year with inadequate retained earnings or thin-capitalisation indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory financial statements, management accounts, solvency and liquidity affidavit of the board, dividend declaration minutes, SARS dividends tax 34B return, shareholder loan amortisation schedule, transfer-pricing file, and authorised-dealer capital-import registration evidence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity subscriptions and shareholder loans must be routed via SWIFT MT103 to the (Pty) Ltd's account held at the SARB authorised dealer. Each wire must clearly reference the legal entity name, the underlying shareholder, and the purpose code for inward direct investment or intercompany loan. The authorised dealer will perform FICA verification, check sanctions, and record the inward transfer for SARB balance-of-payments reporting; the bank's transaction reference becomes the capital-import evidence necessary for future dividend, interest, and capital repatriation. Shareholders should not split transfers, should not use personal accounts for company capital, and must ensure the transferred amount matches the share subscription or loan agreement exactly.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Regular outbound import payments to overseas suppliers, especially Chinese condiment and equipment vendors, should be cleared via SWIFT MT103 through the authorised-dealer bank with supporting invoice, purchase order, transport documents, and customs clearance declaration. High-value or documentary trade settlements should use commercial letters of credit (LC) issued by the South African bank and advised through the beneficiary's Chinese correspondent bank. Local supplier payments and merchant settlement are cleared through BankservAfrica's ACB/SAMOS rails, while card transactions for the restaurant's POS operations are settled via the acquiring bank using the major card schemes; dynamic currency conversion should be disabled so settlement is received in Rand without FX slippage.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward foreign exchange contracts (ZAR forwards) with a SARB authorised dealer for documented trade payables and receivables, supported by underlying invoices and with no speculative intent.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for ZAR exposures where the counterparty currency is not fully deliverable in the South African market, executed through a SARB authorised dealer or an approved international correspondent.

Cross-currency swaps between ZAR and foreign currencies for long-term shareholder loan and dividend-remittance exposures, subject to FinSurv-related authorised-dealer standards and the Financial Markets Act reporting requirements, with full documentation of the underlying capital transaction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers CIPC notice and penalty; persistent non-filing listed as delinquent and leads to administrative strike-off/deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Confirmation embedded in the annual return; any shareholding or control changes filed within 10 business days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file accurate beneficial ownership information can result in administrative fines, personal liability, and criminal prosecution under the Companies Amendment Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if Public Interest Score (PIS) is at least 350, or if the company is public/state-owned or subject to ministerial regulatory requirement; independent review required if PIS between 100 and 349; no audit or review if PIS is below 100.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Full IFRS for companies with a mandatory audit; IFRS for SMEs for private companies not required to adopt full IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The CIPC Annual Return must include a declaration of the current beneficial owners and confirm their beneficial interest. Any change in shareholding or control must be filed within 10 business days, and the Register of Beneficial Ownership must be updated. No separate annual UBO filing is required beyond the Annual Return declaration.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800-1,500 for independent review; USD 3,200-8,000 for full statutory audit
